Package gooeygui

Class Panel

java.lang.Object
gooeygui.Component
gooeygui.Panel
public class Panel extends Component
A rectangular container that holds other components. Panels are useful for grouping components so they can be shown, hidden, enabled, or disabled together, and for building the pages of a TabbedPane.

The positions of components added to a panel are measured from the top-left corner of the panel, not the window.


 Panel settings = new Panel(0, 0, 400, 300);
 settings.addComponent(new Label("Volume", 20, 20, 100, 30));
 window.addComponent(settings);
 settings.setActive(false);  // hides the panel and everything in it
 settings.setEnabled(false); // grays out everything in the panel

  • Constructor Details

    • Panel

      public Panel(int x, int y, int width, int height)
      Constructs an empty panel. If the panel will be used as a tab in a TabbedPane, the tabbed pane sets its position and size automatically, so the values given here are ignored.
      Parameters:
      x - the x-coordinate of the top-left corner, in pixels
      y - the y-coordinate of the top-left corner, in pixels
      width - the width of the panel, in pixels (at least 1)
      height - the height of the panel, in pixels (at least 1)
      Throws:
      GooeyGUIException - if width or height is less than 1

  • Method Details

    • addComponent

      public void addComponent(Component component)
      Adds a component to this panel. The component's (x, y) position is measured from the top-left corner of the panel. If this panel is disabled, the new component is disabled too.
      Parameters:
      component - the component to add
      Throws:
      GooeyGUIException - if component is null, has already been added somewhere, or is this panel (or a panel containing this one)

    • setEnabled

      public void setEnabled(boolean isEnabled)
      Enables or disables this panel and every component inside it. Enabling the panel again restores each inner component to its own setting, so a component you disabled yourself stays disabled.
      Overrides:
      setEnabled in class Component
      Parameters:
      isEnabled - true to let the user interact with the panel's contents, false to gray them all out
